citation.authors: Ooi CP, Yassin Z, Hamid TA

cited_by.title: Bush teas and herbal remedies (cerasee, bitter leaf) with medicines

record.population: 479 adults with type 2 diabetes in four randomised trials of Momordica charantia (bitter gourd, cerasee)
record.design: Cochrane systematic review of randomised trials, up to three months
record.finding: No significant difference in glycaemic control against placebo, and none against metformin or glibenclamide in reliable measures. Risk of bias was generally high. No serious adverse effects were reported in any trial. The authors conclude there is insufficient evidence.
record.note: Trials were of preparations of the plant in other populations; none was a tea made at home.

cited_by.title: Type 2 diabetes risk and blood sugar

record.population: 479 adults with type 2 diabetes in four trials of Momordica charantia (bitter gourd, cerasee)
record.design: Cochrane systematic review of randomised trials, up to three months
record.finding: No significant difference in glycaemic control against placebo, and no significant change against metformin or glibenclamide in reliable measures. Risk of bias was generally high and only two trials were full peer-reviewed papers. The authors conclude there is insufficient evidence.
record.note: Trials were not in people of African descent; they test the plant, not a Black-specific use.
